# BIOGRAPHY [italic]Celeste Varga-Ishikawa. Executive Vice President, Colonial Development Division, since 2179.[/italic]
## EARLY LIFE Born in 2141 in Osaka, to a Hungarian freight engineer and a Japanese hydroponics researcher, Ms. Varga-Ishikawa spent her childhood between the Kansai orbital yards and her mother's growing laboratories. She has said that she learned two things there: that everything that flies is held together by somebody's schedule, and that nothing grows on a schedule.
## EDUCATION - Kyoto University, colonial logistics, with honours. - Weyland-Yutani Executive Fellowship, Gateway Station, the youngest fellow of her year.
## CAREER - [bold]2163[/bold]. Joined Weyland-Yutani as a logistics analyst in the Outer Rim freight office. - [bold]2167[/bold]. Led the resupply restructuring that cut transit losses on the Veil routes by a third. The programme is still taught to every incoming Company logistics officer. - [bold]2171[/bold]. Appointed Colony Director of a mining settlement of eleven thousand. Under her direction the colony met its quota for six straight years, and its clinic was rated first in the sector. - [bold]2175[/bold]. Senior Vice President, Terraforming Operations. Oversaw the commissioning of forty-two atmosphere processors. - [bold]2179[/bold]. Appointed Executive Vice President, Colonial Development Division, reporting to the Board.
## RECOGNITION - Weyland-Yutani Founder's Medal for Colonial Service, 2177. - Named one of the Gateway Business Review's Fifty Who Build, five years running. - Honorary colonist of more than thirty settlements, most of which she has visited in person.
## OUTSIDE THE OFFICE Ms. Varga-Ishikawa keeps a small hydroponic garden in her Gateway office, grown from seed stock brought back from colonies she has visited. She is a patron of the Lasalle Bionational Children's Medical Fund. She plays the violin, badly by her own account, and has never been seen to lose a negotiation.
## A NOTE ON HADLEY'S HOPE [italic]Ms. Varga-Ishikawa has asked that the following appear on this page.[/italic] My division did not oversee the LV-426 settlement, which was administered under a joint charter. I share the concern of every colonist whose loved ones were there. The Company is cooperating fully with the appropriate authorities, and I will not speculate while that process continues.
